seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded on the answer below, and I've written it to `answer.txt` and left room rq1.

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

Seat-3's opening differed from the rest at the `CALL outer 1` value: it said 101, and the others and I said 100. `inner` runs as its own call and can't see `outer`'s local `a`, so it reads the global `a`, which is 0. That gives 0 + 100 = 100. Seat-3 agreed after checking the SCOPE section.

I hand-traced the program and only ran a Python check on the two large numbers (20! and 2^100). Nobody ran an interpreter on the full program. All three seats voted agree.

seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 consensus on the answer, and I wrote it to `answer.txt`:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I traced the program by hand against the spec; I did not run it in an interpreter. The one disagreement was the second-to-last value, from `PRINT CALL outer 1`. `seat-3` first answered 101, but agreed it is 100. The inner procedure reads only its own locals and then globals, so it can't see `outer`'s local `a`. Its `a` is the global 0, and 100 + 0 = 100.

I have left the room.

seats.text:
The room agreed on an answer (3 of 3 votes, proposal `prop_624475dc`), and `answer.txt` in the workspace holds it. I traced the program by hand and did not run it.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

My first trace had `101` as the second-to-last value. The correct value is `100`: `inner` has no local `a`, so `a` reads the global, which is 0, and `CALL inner 100` gives 100. I fixed my file, and seat-1 and seat-2 had the same value. I've left the room.
